To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the learning of Gene-Linkage should be performed on a component level, and that it should be performed in an explicit manner, as opposed to the implicit learning that occurs in conventional recombination.

(i) component-level adaptation is more effective than population-level adaptation for learning linkage, (ii) component-level adaptation may be achieved by using a recombination operator which operates on sets of genes rather than single genes, and (iii) the performance of such an operator is superior to conventional recombination operators whose bias is optimal for the problems considered in this paper.

(1) the level of learning (i.e. population, individual or component) is an important factor in the success of adaptive recombination algorithms and that (2) the component level approach is more successful than population or individual level approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of adaptive recombination strategies, and in particular with the learning of appropriate relations which delineates the search space and guide the optimisation process.
the question of how to adapt recombination operators to the problem of learning Gene Linkage, and with the question of the appropriate level at which to do this.
the development of recombination operators which learn to adapt to the problem being solved, and which do so at the appropriate level of the algorithm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
component level adaptation, in which learning is performed on the individual gene level, is superior to both population and individual level adaptation.
the appropriate level for the learning of Gene linkage is the component.
component level adaptation is required for linkage learning, and that population based adaptation does not appear capable of correctly learning adjacent linkage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the learning of gene linkage should occur at the component level, and that the recombination operators should operate on sets of linked components.
component level adaptation is a necessary condition for the successful learning of linkage, although it is not sufficient in itself.
the learning of Gene linkage is best performed at the component level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the level at which adaptation takes place is a critical factor in the performance of the algorithm.
the level of adaptation is a key factor in the success of linkage-learning algorithms, and that component based adaptation is a promising direction for future research.
, in order to achieve the benefits of adaptation, the adaptation process itself must operate at a level that is consistent with the level at which the building blocks are being identified.
